texts: mixed: nothing is lost — Marra is typed a cousin and linked to Meren by the generic possessive link — but that link runs one way only, so "who is Meren's cousin?" answers while "who is Marra's cousin?" finds nothing. Since cousinhood is mutual, state it symmetrically instead: "Marra Tallowhand and Meren Tallowhand are cousins." — that yields a relation the reasoner can read in both directions.
good. the tending, the named tender and the "harbor wall station" kind (with its station genus) are all covered, and no kind atom is invented for the name.

mixed: every word is accounted for, but "detailed" and "nightly" end up parked in a per-log rule that lies dormant — no individual log is ever introduced, so nothing can answer "are her logs detailed?". Rewrite it as a single-log habit: "Marra Tallowhand keeps a detailed log every night." — "detailed" then sits directly on the log, and "nightly" becomes an ordinary nightly recurrence on the keeping.

bad: the whole consulting event is packed into one reduced-strength conjunction instead of separate atoms, so an ordinary "who consults the logs?" query cannot match it at all; and "often" has no licensed home when the actor is one specific body, so the frequency is either smuggled into that lowered strength or lost outright. Rewrite with a plural actor, which gives the frequency somewhere to live: "Council members often consult Marra Tallowhand's logs." If the Council must stay a single actor, drop "often" ("The Council consults Marra Tallowhand's logs.") and state the rate in a stated period instead, since only a named period or rate can be encoded.
